topic: Nickelodeon Child Actor Speaks Out on Reality of Residual Checks
headline: FORMER NICKELODEON CHILD STAR SPEAKS OUT ON 'TOXIC' RESIDUAL CHECKS, CALLS FOR INVESTIGATION INTO KIDS TV INDUSTRY
summary: A Nickelodeon child actor has spoken out about the reality of residual checks, amid a documentary series 'Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV' that details the behind-the-scenes world of children's television. The series has sparked a conversation about child actors and their experiences. Some actors have shared their own stories and reactions to the documentary, with some expressing support for an investigation into Nickelodeon.

sections.paragraph: The documentary television series 'Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV' explores the toxic behind-the-scenes world of children's television programs from the 1990s to the 2000s, with a focus on Dan Schneider's tenure at Nickelodeon. The series, which consists of five episodes, premiered on Investigation Discovery and was simultaneously released on HBO Max and Discovery+. It received positive reviews from audiences and critics, with a 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and an average rating of 7.6/10. The series sparked conversations about the treatment of child actors and the darker side of the entertainment industry, with some former Nickelodeon stars, such as Kel Mitchell and Allie DiMeco, sharing their own experiences and allegations. The show's release also led to calls for Nickelodeon to investigate the allegations and to provide a safer environment for child actors. The series was a commercial success, becoming the most streamed television series in the United States from March 18 to March 25, 2024.

sections.paragraph: The shift to streaming has significantly impacted the business of TV shows, with many being cut due to cost-saving measures. This has resulted in the disappearance of shows, leaving actors and writers uncertain about their work being seen again and affecting their residual payments. The Writers Guild of America (WGA) is seeking better residual rates, higher minimum pay rates, and improved financial security in its upcoming contract negotiations. A potential strike could have significant economic implications, as the last writers' strike in 2008 cost the California economy an estimated $2 billion. The issue of residuals is particularly pressing, with some writers reporting significantly lower residual checks for streaming shows compared to traditional broadcast shows. As the industry continues to evolve, the fate of TV shows and the livelihoods of those involved remain uncertain.

sections.paragraph: The COVID-19 pandemic has had a significant social impact on mental health, with many individuals experiencing increased anxiety, stress, and trauma. For those who have had painful life experiences in the past, the pandemic may trigger memories of past traumas, leading to long-term mental health conditions such as PTSD. Some people, like Lindsey Higgins, have reported a resurgence in PTSD symptoms, while others, like Susan Kemp, have developed social anxiety and germaphobia-based obsessive-compulsive behaviors. The pandemic has also highlighted the need for increased support for children's mental health, with many requiring one-to-one professional help. Furthermore, the uncertainty surrounding the pandemic has tapped into humanity's fundamental fear of the unknown, with people varying greatly in their perceptions of uncertainty and responses to it. This fear of the unknown can lead to heightened stress responses and have significant consequences for one's health and wellbeing.

sections.paragraph: The Hollywood actors' strike, which lasted for 118 days, has come to a tentative end with a deal between the Sag-Aftra union and the Alliance of Motion Picture and Television Producers (AMPTP). The agreement includes notable provisions such as minimum pay, streaming-based bonuses, and consent and compensation guarantees for the use of AI likenesses. The deal has been hailed as a historic breakthrough by union leadership and the AMPTP, with the union's president, Fran Drescher, stating that studios now need to ask for permission for everything. The contract, reportedly worth $1 billion over three years, also secured 'above pattern' minimum wage increases. The strike, which involved around 160,000 Sag-Aftra members, including actors, video game performers, and YouTube influencers, was called due to a breakdown in negotiations with the AMPTP, with issues such as pay, residuals, and the impact of AI being major points of contention.
